contractSource: Description: "Calculate electric motor power, current, torque, and efficiency. Supports HP to kW conversion..." FAQ: "For a three-phase AC motor: Output Power (kW) = √3 × Voltage (V) × Current (A) × Power Factor × Efficiency ÷ 1000"; how-to: "Select motor type and phase — choose single-phase or three-phase AC motor, or DC motor" and "Input ... power factor".
groundTruth: Mechanical shaft power P = 2π·N·T / 60 (N in rpm, T in N·m). 1 mechanical horsepower = 745.7 W.

cases.note: Torque and speed — a formula the tool should get right.

cases.derivation: 1 mechanical hp = 550 ft·lbf/s = 745.7 W. 10 hp × 745.7 = 7,457 W = 7.457 kW (the rounded 746 W/hp gives 7.46 kW, within tolerance).

cases.note: The page promises phase selection and a power-factor input for electrical calculations.
cases.derivation: The how-to tells users to "Select motor type and phase" and enter "power factor"; without them the page's own FAQ example (7.5 kW three-phase motor, 415 V, PF 0.85, 90% efficiency → 13.7 A) cannot be reproduced: √3 × 415 × 13.7 × 0.85 × 0.90 = 7.53 kW, whereas V × I × η alone gives 415 × 13.7 × 0.90 = 5.12 kW.

expect.what: a power factor input, as the how-to promises
a single/three-phase selector, as the how-to promises
